:::{#def-observation-loss}
#### Loss of a fitted model on an observation

The **loss** of a [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) $\fitted$ on an observation $(\predvar_{\iobs}, \outvar_{\iobs})$
is the cost, under a [loss function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-loss-function) $\loss$,
of its prediction $\predvalf{\predvar_{\iobs}}$ of the outcome $\outvar_{\iobs}$:

$$
\obsloss{\iobs}\paren{\fitted} \eqdef \lossf{\outvar_{\iobs}, \predvalf{\predvar_{\iobs}}}.
$$ {#eq-observation-loss}

The subscript names the observation, a member of a family of losses,
and the parentheses hold the fitted model the loss is evaluated at.
The index $*$ names the new observation $(\newpredvar, \newoutvar)$,
so $\obsloss{*}\paren{\fitted} = \lossf{\newoutvar, \predvalf{\newpredvar}}$.
When the [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) is clear from context, we write $\obsloss{\iobs}$ for $\obsloss{\iobs}\paren{\fitted}$.

:::
